name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 1: Fullness at the two points where the breath arises
method_summary: The verse describes, without a command, that the supreme (Parā), whose nature is emission (visarga), sounds forth as prāṇa above and as jīva below; the practitioner is implicitly asked to attend to the two places where these arise (it follows the question 'by what means?' in v.23, and carries no imperative verb).
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, of thought-free mind, heroes of lofty self (VBT 157-159).
notes: Text-derived summary of GRETIL verse(s) 24; the skeleton entry's name and numbering are kept.
signs_of_progress: The verse says that by filling (bharaṇa) at the two places of arising there is a standing in fullness (bharitā sthiti).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 2: The two voids at the turning points of the breath
method_summary: The verse describes the breath (marut), whether inside or outside, as not turning back from the pair of spaces (viyad-yugma); the practitioner is implicitly asked to attend to this pair of spaces at the two ends of the breath (no imperative verb).
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, of thought-free mind, heroes of lofty self (VBT 157-159).
notes: Text-derived summary of GRETIL verse(s) 25; the skeleton entry's name and numbering are kept.
signs_of_progress: The verse says that in this way, Bhairavī, the form of Bhairava and Bhairavī is disclosed.

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 3: Suspension of the breath-power in the centre
method_summary: The verse describes the breath-power (śakti in the form of marut) as neither going out nor entering, the middle having expanded; the practitioner is implicitly asked to rest in that middle without forming thought-constructs (nirvikalpatā).
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, of thought-free mind, heroes of lofty self (VBT 157-159).
notes: Text-derived summary of GRETIL verse(s) 26; the skeleton entry's name and numbering are kept.
signs_of_progress: The verse says that by this, in the middle, Bhairava-nature (bhairava-rūpatā) comes about.

method_summary: About the moment at the end of a breath that has been held, expelled or drawn in, at which the one called 'the Peaceful' (Śānta) is said to shine, peaceful through Śakti; recorded as a summary only because it concerns breath retention.
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, of thought-free mind, heroes of lofty self (VBT 157-159).
notes: Text-derived summary of GRETIL verse(s) 27; the skeleton entry's name and numbering are kept. Restricted: summary only; the text gives no caution of its own.

prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, of thought-free mind, heroes of lofty self (VBT 157-159).

prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, of thought-free mind, heroes of lofty self (VBT 157-159).
notes: Text-derived summary of GRETIL verse(s) 121; the skeleton entry's name and numbering are kept.
signs_of_progress: The verse says that from that one becomes Śiva.

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 96: The voidness of all else when one object is known
method_summary: The verse speaks of another object being known and voidness (śūnyatā) in all objects; the practitioner is asked to meditate on that very voidness with the mind.
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, of thought-free mind, heroes of lofty self (VBT 157-159).
notes: Text-derived summary of GRETIL verse(s) 122; the skeleton entry's name and numbering are kept.
signs_of_progress: The verse says that even the known object is quieted (praśāmyati).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 97: Purity and impurity
method_summary: The verse says that the purity thought of by those of little knowledge, in the vision of Śambhu, is 'not pure' and the practitioner is asked to be thought-free.
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, of thought-free mind, heroes of lofty self (VBT 157-159).
notes: Text-derived summary of GRETIL verse(s) 123; the skeleton entry's name and numbering are kept.
signs_of_progress: The verse says that therefore, being thought-free, one becomes happy.

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 98: Bhairava in ordinary things
method_summary: The verse states that Bhairava's being (bhāva) is everywhere, an object of experience even among ordinary things, and that there is nothing beyond it; the practitioner is implicitly asked to see it so.
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, of thought-free mind, heroes of lofty self (VBT 157-159).
notes: Text-derived summary of GRETIL verse(s) 124; the skeleton entry's name and numbering are kept.
signs_of_progress: The verse calls this the non-dual way (advayā gati).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 99: Equality toward friend and foe
method_summary: The practitioner is asked to know that, because of the completeness (paripūrṇatva) of Brahman, one is equal toward enemy and friend and equal in honour and dishonour.
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, of thought-free mind, heroes of lofty self (VBT 157-159).
notes: Text-derived summary of GRETIL verse(s) 125; the skeleton entry's name and numbering are kept.
signs_of_progress: The verse says that knowing so one would be happy.

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 100: Neither attachment nor aversion
method_summary: The practitioner is asked not to cultivate aversion anywhere and not to cultivate attachment anywhere.
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, of thought-free mind, heroes of lofty self (VBT 157-159).
notes: Text-derived summary of GRETIL verse(s) 126; the skeleton entry's name and numbering are kept.
signs_of_progress: The verse says that when freed from attachment and aversion, in the middle Brahman moves (prasarpati).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 101: The unknowable and the void as Bhairava
method_summary: The practitioner is asked to contemplate as Bhairava all that is unknowable, ungraspable, void, and going to non-being (abhāva).
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, of thought-free mind, heroes of lofty self (VBT 157-159).
notes: Text-derived summary of GRETIL verse(s) 127; the skeleton entry's name and numbering are kept.
signs_of_progress: The verse says that at its end the arising of awakening (bodha) comes.

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 102: The mind in outer space
method_summary: The practitioner is asked to place the mind in outer space, which is eternal, supportless, void, all-pervading and free of reckoning (kalanā).
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, of thought-free mind, heroes of lofty self (VBT 157-159).
notes: Text-derived summary of GRETIL verse(s) 128; the skeleton entry's name and numbering are kept.
signs_of_progress: The verse says that one would enter the spaceless (nirākāśa).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 103: Letting go of each object the moment the mind goes to it
method_summary: Wherever the mind goes, the practitioner is asked to abandon that very thing at that very moment, by the mind itself, by not letting it stay (anavasthiti).
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, of thought-free mind, heroes of lofty self (VBT 157-159).
notes: Text-derived summary of GRETIL verse(s) 129; the skeleton entry's name and numbering are kept.
signs_of_progress: The verse says that one then becomes waveless (nistaraṅga).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 104: Continuous utterance of the word 'Bhairava'
method_summary: The verse gives an analysis of the word 'Bhairava' (bha, ra, va): 'through fear he makes all resound, he gives all, he pervades the whole'; the practitioner is asked to utter the word Bhairava continuously.
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, of thought-free mind, heroes of lofty self (VBT 157-159).
notes: Text-derived summary of GRETIL verse(s) 130; the skeleton entry's name and numbering are kept.
signs_of_progress: The verse says that from continuous utterance of the word there is Śiva.

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 105: At the thought 'I' and 'mine'
method_summary: In the course of taking up notions such as 'I' and 'this is mine', the verse says the mind goes to the supportless; the practitioner is implicitly asked to meditate on that.
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, of thought-free mind, heroes of lofty self (VBT 157-159).
notes: Text-derived summary of GRETIL verse(s) 131; the skeleton entry's name and numbering are kept.

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 106: Contemplating the words 'eternal', 'all-pervading', 'supportless'
method_summary: The practitioner is asked to meditate at every moment on the words 'eternal, all-pervading, supportless, pervasive, lord of all', according to their meanings.
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, of thought-free mind, heroes of lofty self (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 107: 'What reality has a magic show?'
method_summary: The practitioner is asked to hold firmly: 'all this stands without reality (atattva), like a magic show; what reality has a magic show?'
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, of thought-free mind, heroes of lofty self (VBT 157-159).

method_summary: The verse states, as a reflection: for the unchanging (nirvikāra) self, where is knowledge and where is action? Outer things depend on knowledge; therefore this world is void (śūnya).
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, of thought-free mind, heroes of lofty self (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 109: 'No bondage, no liberation for me'
method_summary: The practitioner is asked to hold: 'for me there is no bondage and no liberation; these are bugbears (vibhīṣikā) for the frightened; this [world] is a reflection of the intellect (buddhi), like that of the sun in waters.'
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, of thought-free mind, heroes of lofty self (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 110: Withdrawing from the senses into the self
method_summary: The verse states that all contact with pleasure, pain and the like comes through the doors of the senses; the practitioner is asked accordingly to abandon the senses.
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, of thought-free mind, heroes of lofty self (VBT 157-159).

method_summary: The verse states that everything is illumined by knowledge and that the self is the illuminator through everything, and that knowledge and the knowable are contemplated as one.
